physical_harm: The deceased suffered multiple injuries including a crush injury on the left cheek, cut lacerated wounds on the face and neck, and a fracture to the C2 vertebra, which led to his death.
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged, one upheld (Section 302) and one altered to Section 325
motive: Illicit relationship between appellant No.1 and the deceased's wife
key_evidence_accepted: The three witnesses namely PWs 8, 18 and 16 have clearly testified about the sequence of events leading to the death of the deceased which version has been found to be reliable by the courts below. The medical evidence adduced at the trial supports the ocular version.
witness_credibility: The fact that the deceased suspected his wife's fidelity and an illicit intimacy with appellant No.1 is sufficiently proved from the deposition of the widow of the deceased (PW-16), and the other two witnesses (PWs 8 and 18). The presence of the two eye witnesses on the spot at the time of occurrence in a place like a bus stand is in no way abnormal to cast any doubt about their credibility.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 30th August, 2006; Trial judgment: 15.11.2011; High Court decision: 15th November, 2011; Supreme Court decision: JULY 5, 2013
legal_representation: H. Chandra Sekhar for the Appellants; C.B. Gururaj, V.N. Raghupathy for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: conviction and sentence under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and Section 506 read with Section 34 IPC; High Court: affirmed conviction and sentence under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC, set aside conviction and sentence under Section 506 read with Section 34 IPC; Supreme Court: dismissed appeal of appellant No.1 and partly allowed appeal of appellant No.2
prosecution_argument: The prosecution case proved its case as regards the sequence of events leading to the death of the deceased, beyond reasonable doubt. The witnesses, including the eye-witness, medical evidence as well as FSL report support the prosecution case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no evidence that appellant No.2 intended to cause death or shared intention to cause death with appellant No.1. The prosecution has not even alleged a motive against appellant No.2. The motive based on illicit relationship between appellant No.1 and the wife of the deceased could hardly be attributed to appellant No.2.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that for a conviction under Section 302 IPC, there must be evidence of intention to cause death or shared intention to cause death. The court also relied on the principle that the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the conviction of appellant No.2 was altered to s.325 IPC, and his sentence already undergone was considered sufficient.
